introduction: Here, we dive deeper into the 5 major divisions of the Plant Kingdom and understand how plant structures (like roots and stems) modify themselves for survival.

core_concepts.title: 1. Thallophyta (Algae)
core_concepts.description:
The most primitive plants. Their body is a 'Thallus' (not differentiated into roots, stems, or leaves). They are mostly aquatic. 
Examples: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Chara.

core_concepts.title: 2. Bryophyta (Mosses)
core_concepts.description:
These are called the **'Amphibians of the Plant Kingdom'** because they live on land but absolutely require water for sexual reproduction (sperms need to swim). 
Examples: Riccia, Marchantia, Moss/Funaria.

core_concepts.title: 3. Pteridophyta (Ferns)
core_concepts.description:
These are the **'First true land plants'**. They are the first to develop vascular tissues (Xylem and Phloem). They have true roots, stems, and leaves but do not produce seeds. 
Examples: Ferns, Marsilea.

core_concepts.title: 4. Gymnosperms (Naked Seeds)
core_concepts.description:
Plants that produce seeds, but the seeds are 'Naked' (not enclosed inside a fruit). They are usually tall, evergreen woody trees. 
Examples: Cycas, Pinus (Pine trees), Cedar.

core_concepts.title: 5. Angiosperms (Covered Seeds)
core_concepts.description:
The most advanced and highly evolved plants. They produce **Flowers**, and their seeds are safely enclosed inside **Fruits**. 
Divided into two types based on cotyledons (seed leaves): 
1. Monocots: Single seed leaf (e.g., Wheat, Rice, Grass). 
2. Dicots: Two seed leaves (e.g., Pea, Mango, Gram).

important_entities.name: Plant Modifications
important_entities.key_fact: Potato is a Stem, not a Root!
important_entities.significance:
A highly tested exam concept: 
- Modified Stems: Potato, Onion, Ginger, Garlic, Turmeric. 
- Modified Roots: Carrot, Radish, Turnip, Sweet Potato. 
(Examiners love tricking students into thinking Potato is a root because it grows underground).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Does the 'Dark Reaction' (Calvin Cycle) happen at night? NO! It is called 'dark' only because it doesn't *directly* require light, but it still happens during the daytime using the energy (ATP) generated by the Light Reaction.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: T = Thallophyta, B = Bryophyta, P = Pteridophyta, G = Gymnosperms, A = Angiosperms.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC/State PCS favorite: 'Which group of plants is known as the amphibians of the plant kingdom?' Answer: Bryophyta.
